summary: Feed s052_single to SIEM is degraded due to 2.1% packet drops (52 of 2419 TCP packets with missing data, threshold 1%) - all other checks (duplicates, encrypted share, VLAN, one-way, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream SPAN/mirror port oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion causing tail drops under burst. Evidenced by TCP sequence gaps across 52 packets; SPAN copies are best-effort and drop when source exceeds destination/broker capacity, unlike passive TAP.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete flows with gaps in TCP streams; event correlation, session reassembly and detection coverage will be degraded with missed alerts and incomplete forensic timelines, even though SIEM does not require full payload or bidirectional traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Passive TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy eliminating SPAN oversubscription drops. Ensures complete traffic reaches packet broker and 1G SIEM port. If TAP already present, verify broker buffer/capacity and add filtering to prevent downstream drops.
